title: add-adaptive-tool-routing-playbook-and-minirunner-quickstart
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: teams building multi-tool agents often need deterministic rules for choosing which tool to call under varying latency/cost constraints. This quickstart introduces an 'Adaptive Tool Routing' playbook and a lightweight 'minirunner' sample that demonstrates policy-based routing (latency-first, cost-first, fallback chains) plus typed tool contracts and a small TS/Go runtime shim. What this PR adds: - A step-by-step playbook (quickstarts/adaptive-tool-routing/README.md) explaining adaptive routing patterns, policy knobs, telemetry hooks, and test prompts. - A minirunner sample in TypeScript (minirunner/ts/) that implements a pluggable router, a fake-local tool adapter (search/summarize/calc), and a typed contract linter (JSON Schema). - A compact Go runtime example (minirunner/go/) showing how to embed the same routing logic in a compiled binary for edge deployments. - Docs snippets and API examples added to docs/snippets/tool-contracts.md and docs/snippets/policy-templates.md. - CI smoke tests and a small e2e harness that exercises canary routing and fallback behavior. Checklist: - [x] Quickstart README with goals, expected outcomes, and guided exercises - [x] Example tool contracts (typed) and schema validation - [x] TS + Go minirunner samples with README and run scripts - [x] Instrumentation examples: metrics tags and tracing spans - [x] CI smoke tests and basic linting - [x] Reviewed and approved by reviewers Usage summary: Follow quickstarts/adaptive-tool-routing/README.md to run live scenarios (local Docker-compose target for the TS minirunner, and a makefile-backed build for the Go binary). The playbook includes a section on migrating an existing earlier agent to use the adaptive router by mapping existing tool bindings to the typed-contract format and enabling a canary routing policy. Compatibility: Works with Redwood runtime >= 0.18.0 and SDKs (ts >= 1.7.0, go >= 0.4.2). Notes: This PR focuses on examples and docs; no changes to core runtime. The minirunner intentionally simulates tool latency and error conditions to make testing deterministic.
